newsitem.title: USA: U.S high-yield debt issuance stifled by cash flows.
newsitem.headline: U.S high-yield debt issuance stifled by cash flows.

text.p: Redemptions of $663 million from high-yield bond mutual funds in the latest reporting week ensures underwriters will face an arduous task to place new junk bonds in the coming week, syndicate officials said.
But that calendar promises to be slight, with only companies in need of immediate financing coming to market, they added.

A two-part offering from Triton Energy Corp, including $200 million each of five- and 30-year debt, may be the sole issue to test the market on Friday. The issue is expected to be priced via Bear Stearns & Co and Salomon Brothers.
Bear Stearns officials were not available for comment.

Deals postponed this week, including $220 million from Bank United Corp, $80 million from Prime Matrix Communications and $150 million from Station Casinos (underwritten by BancAmerica Securities), were not expected to resurface for weeks, sources said, especially after the negative read on Friday of high-yield mutual fund cash flows as measured by AMG Data Services.
Further, buysiders and syndicates both said even top tier credits will have to settle for higher borrowing costs.

"If I were managing a fund I'd have a hard time buying right now," conceded one syndicate source at a large New York investment bank. "If you're in for a primary issue you can basically dictate the terms because the only people that are coming to market now are those that need to get deals done to complete an acquisition or some other project."
There is one glimmer of light for high-yield debt issuance: one syndicate source said demand for high-yields may grow should talk of more collateralized bond obligations (CBOs) come to fruition.
Friday's release of jobs data in which non-farm payrolls grew by 175,000 in March exacerbated fears of higher borrowing rates for both junk and investment grade debt, players said.

High-grade debt syndicates reported a still queasy tone to the new issue market despite the relative stability to secondary market spreads. Reflecting the softness, GTE's $500 million issue of Thursday was bid three basis points wider than the issue price of 67 basis points off the curve.
"There were a couple of deals withdrawn or changed and, of the deals that were done, to say that 60 percent was placed would be generous," one dealer said of deal placement.

Looking ahead: buyers said they had been waiting for the passing of employment data to return to market, which may portend stability for next week. The calendar is slow to build, sources said, but they noted J.C. Penney Co's $2.0 billion multi-tranche issue has completed a roadshow and will be priced via Credit Suisse First Boston next week.
